title: Grateful Dead Live at Veterans Auditorium on 1969-06-28
lineage: SBD > MR > Cassette > DAT > CD > Kenwood TrueX > EAC > shn V3 (seekable)

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a classic ’69 setlist with smoking Doin' That Rag, King Bee, Turn On Your Love Light and stellar country numbers.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its crisp, clear soundboard quality that lets every instrument shine, even if a touch of Dolby noise reduction would improve it. Musically the show is hailed as a quintessential 1969 performance – Jerry’s steel on Slewfoot and Silver Threads, Phil’s booming bass, Bob’s soulful vocals and Mickey’s double‑drum magic drive an energetic, roots‑infused set that deadheads describe as unforgettable.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high reviewer scores (average ~4.4) and overwhelmingly positive comments about both the performance and sound quality outweigh a single low‑rating complaint.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with high levels; some reviewers note minor noise‑reduction (Dolby) needs but overall the sound is exceptionally clean.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A classic ’69 setlist that moves smoothly from country‑flavored numbers to bluesy jams, showcasing the band’s transition from anthem‑rock to organic American roots music.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Plays steel guitar on Slewfoot and Silver Threads; vocal stretches praised; pedal work noted as exceptional.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass described as “rocks the bass like it's a baby in his arms,” delivering powerful low‑end support.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals called youthful, soulful and central to the cowboy/roots feel of the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s double‑drum magic noted; drums described as firecracker‑like and energetic.
